message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph on rural interstates).
• In cities: 25–35 mph in residential areas, 35–45 mph on main streets.
• “No‑speed‑limit” zones (e.g., 20 mph) are common in downtowns. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• Texas has a “no‑seat‑belt” law for drivers over 18. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | | **Alcohol & Driving** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is DUI.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC 0.02 % or higher).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light = stop; green = go; yellow = prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop at the line or crosswalk.
• Yield signs give right‑of‑way to vehicles already in the intersection. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians always have right‑of‑way at crosswalks.
• School buses stopping for children have absolute right‑of‑way. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Passing on the right is illegal unless the left lane is occupied or the driver is turning left. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, bus stops, or within 20 ft of a crosswalk.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited unless marked.
• Disabled parking requires a valid permit. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display a valid registration sticker.
• Towing of abandoned vehicles requires a permit from the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT). | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles must wear helmets (mandatory for riders under 18).
• Commercial vehicles must follow specific weight and safety regulations. | | **Penalties & Enforcement** | • Fines vary by offense; repeat offenders face higher penalties.
• Points are added to the driver’s record; 12 points in 36 months can lead to license suspension.
• Texas uses a “point system” for most moving‑violation offenses. | ### Where to Find the Full Text - **Texas Transportation Code** – Chapter 545 covers motor vehicle traffic laws. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Provides driver’s handbook and updates on statutes. - **TxDOT** – Offers resources on road safety, signage, and enforcement guidelines. ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for safety. 2. **Keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. 3. **Avoid distractions** – no texting or handheld phone use. 4. **Know the right‑of‑way rules** – especially at uncontrolled intersections. 5. **Stay alert for school buses** – they have absolute right‑of‑way when stopping. If you need more detailed information on a specific law or want to check recent changes, let me know!
